_description: Foundational node taxonomy for VFX artists building Unreal materials that interact with Niagara. Use this as a priority map when deciding which material nodes matter most for common production VFX work.
overview: A production VFX material is usually built from a small set of high-value nodes reused in different combinations. A strong VFX artist does not need to memorize every node in the editor. They need to know which node families solve data flow, texture motion, masking, deformation, and natural variation first.

categories.why_it_matters: These nodes carry data from Niagara into the material. Without them, the material cannot react cleanly to lifetime, tint, alpha, or per-particle control values.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Read particle RGB and Alpha directly from Niagara.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: If Niagara is expected to drive tint or fade, keep Particle Color in the graph and make sure its Alpha influences the opacity path or the emissive path when additive blending is involved.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Send up to four float channels from Niagara into the material.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Prefer stable shared channel naming across a material family so Niagara-side parameter setup stays reusable. For the shared fire and smoke ParticleSubUV workflow, use PowerEmissive, FadeDistance, CameraDpthFade, Power with default values R=1, G=1, B=1, A=2.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Read normalized lifetime from 0 to 1 directly in the material.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Use Particle Relative Time when timing should live inside the material. If Niagara already owns the fade curve, do not duplicate the same timing logic in the material unless there is a specific artistic reason.

common_mistakes: omitting Particle Color and then wondering why Niagara color or alpha curves do not affect the material
using Dynamic Parameter channels with inconsistent naming from one material to the next
duplicating lifetime logic in both Niagara and the material without a clear reason

categories.display_name: Node dieu khien UV va chuyen dong
categories.why_it_matters: Most VFX motion is faked through UV movement or frame lookup rather than heavy geometry simulation.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Scroll texture UVs in a chosen direction.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: When a look needs cheap continuous flow, try Panner before inventing a more complex graph.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Rotate texture UVs over time or by a control value.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Use Rotator when the visual needs circular or orbiting motion instead of linear drift.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Control UV tiling and coordinate scale.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Treat TextureCoordinate as the root scaling control for most sampled textures. It is usually the first stop for fixing tiling density before touching more advanced nodes.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Read flipbook frames from a sprite sheet using Niagara SubUV playback.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: If the motion is stored in the atlas frames, prefer ParticleSubUV over trying to fake that motion with panners. Verify the Niagara renderer SubUV grid before debugging the material.

common_mistakes: using a plain Texture Sample where ParticleSubUV is required for a real flipbook sheet
driving motion with too many unrelated panners so the read becomes noisy instead of directional
forgetting to match the Niagara renderer SubUV grid to the actual atlas layout

categories.why_it_matters: These nodes define silhouettes, cutoffs, rims, and dissolves. They are often the difference between a readable effect and an amorphous blob.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Create soft radial masks and falloffs.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Use SphereMask when the effect wants a soft center-to-edge radial falloff.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Measure distance between positions or values.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Distance is usually a support node for masks or fields, not the final visual by itself.
If an effect needs readable edges or a magical shell feel, Fresnel is usually a first-choice node.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Push mask contrast cheaply without a full custom setup.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Use CheapContrast when the graph needs a quick contrast push without overbuilding.
Step is for decisive hard cutoffs. Pair it with SmoothStep when aliasing becomes too harsh.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Create a soft threshold between two values.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Prefer SmoothStep when the artist wants threshold control with softer transitions.

common_mistakes: adding noise detail before the main silhouette is readable
using hard Step everywhere and creating ugly aliasing
letting Fresnel become the entire effect instead of supporting the hero shape

categories.why_it_matters: Some VFX need motion in the actual mesh or card shape, not only in texture color. These nodes control that behavior.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Move vertices in world space at the material output stage.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Use World Position Offset when silhouette motion matters. Do not use it as a substitute for texture motion when only the internal pattern needs to move.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Provide outward vertex direction for inflation or directional displacement.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Vertex Normal WS is usually paired with World Position Offset to push geometry outward cleanly.

common_mistakes: using World Position Offset on effects that only need internal texture motion
forgetting that aggressive World Position Offset can break collision expectations or card readability
expecting World Position Offset to solve flipbook timing problems

categories.why_it_matters: Natural-looking VFX need controlled irregularity. Time and noise provide that motion and breakup without manually animating everything.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Create procedural breakup and organic variation.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Noise is a support layer. Use it to enrich the read after the primary silhouette and flow are already working.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Drive continuous animation in the material.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Time by itself is rarely the effect. Pair it with Panner, Sine, Cosine, or UV math.
Use Sine or Cosine for deliberate rhythm. Avoid it when the effect should feel chaotic or stochastic.

common_mistakes: using too much noise and losing the hero read
making oscillation perfectly rhythmic when the effect should feel organic
stacking multiple time-based layers without clear speed separation

cross_reference_playbook.use_with_fire_and_smoke_flipbooks: Pair this taxonomy with Knowledge/Materials/Techniques/particle_subuv_flipbook_fire_smoke.json when building Niagara-driven fire or smoke sheets.
cross_reference_playbook.use_with_fresnel_shell_work: Pair this taxonomy with Knowledge/Materials/Techniques/fresnel.json when the effect read depends on edge glow or shell shaping.
cross_reference_playbook.use_with_uv_flow_materials: Pair this taxonomy with Knowledge/Materials/Techniques/panning_uv.json when the main motion comes from UV scrolling instead of frame playback.
cross_reference_playbook.use_with_portal_or_ring_effects: Pair this taxonomy with Knowledge/Materials/Techniques/portal_ring.json when the hero shape is radial and threshold-driven.
cross_reference_playbook.use_with_advanced_senior_workflows: Pair this taxonomy with Knowledge/Materials/Techniques/vfx_artist_advanced_node_taxonomy.json when the effect also needs depth-aware integration, custom flipbook math, optimization switches, or mesh-animation-aware mapping.

agent_guardrails: Prefer a small readable graph built from these foundational nodes before escalating to Custom or HLSL.
Separate Niagara-owned responsibilities from material-owned responsibilities.
When ParticleSubUV is present, verify the renderer SubUV grid and playback path before blaming the material.
When a fade seems broken, inspect whether the visible energy is coming from Emissive, Opacity, or both.
Do not introduce World Position Offset, heavy noise, or extra masks until the core silhouette and timing are already readable.
